cultural.summary: Cut off wilting shoots and holed fruits with the grub still inside!
cultural.how: Regularly remove and destroy wilted shoot tips and bored fruits until the last harvest; avoid continuous brinjal/potato; uproot and burn old plants; intercrop 2 rows of brinjal with 1 row of coriander or fennel; avoid ratooning.
cultural.evidence: NIPHM-Brinjal. In Kullu, transplanting on 15 May gave the lowest shoot infestation (9.9%); incidence peaks in July-August.

cultural.summary: Give the soil a break from the same plant family!
cultural.how: Avoid growing brinjal, tomato, potato or capsicum in the same field in consecutive seasons; rotate with maize, wheat, rice or soybean.

biological.how: Use 10 pheromone traps per acre for mass trapping (4-5 for monitoring), 10 m apart, from 20 days after transplanting; change lures regularly.

biological.summary: Tiny wasps that eat borer eggs!
biological.how: Release Trichogramma chilonis at 20,000 per acre per week from 21 days after transplanting to crop end; tie cards on sticks 4-5 m apart in the evening.

botanical.summary: The most widely endorsed botanical spray across these crops!
botanical.how: Spray NSKE at 5% (50 ml per litre of water), covering both leaf surfaces.
botanical.frequency: As pests appear, repeat after 10 days
botanical.evidence: 5% is the concentration in the NIPHM packages; they give no preparation recipe, so use a commercial NSKE or follow local KVK instructions.

cultural.summary: Clean the seed of the fungus before sowing!
cultural.how: Take seed from healthy fruits and treat it in hot water at 50 C for 30 minutes.

cultural.summary: Give the soil a break from the same plant family!
cultural.how: Avoid growing brinjal, tomato, potato or capsicum in the same field in consecutive seasons; rotate with maize, wheat, rice or soybean.

cultural.summary: Turn the soil in May-June so sun and birds clear out hiding pests and germs!
cultural.how: Plough deeply and leave the soil exposed to sun for 2-3 weeks before planting.

cultural.summary: The fungus survives on old plant debris!
cultural.how: Destroy diseased debris after harvest and avoid continuous brinjal.
cultural.evidence: NIPHM-Brinjal. Favoured by about 26 C, wet weather and high humidity.

biological.summary: Protect seed and seedlings from day one!
biological.how: Seed: 5 g Trichoderma viride 1% WP per kg seed as a thin paste, shade-dry before sowing. Seedlings: dip roots for 15 minutes in 10 g per litre of water before transplanting.

cultural.summary: Remove infected plants early to protect the rest!
cultural.how: Uproot infected plants as soon as you see symptoms and destroy them away from the field (not in compost).

cultural.summary: Datura, Catharanthus and Argemone shelter the disease!
cultural.how: Remove solanaceous weed hosts around the field, plant tolerant varieties (e.g. JC-1, JC-2) and control leafhoppers.

botanical.frequency: As pests appear, repeat after 10 days
botanical.evidence: 5% is the concentration in the NIPHM packages; they give no preparation recipe, so use a commercial NSKE or follow local KVK instructions.

cultural.summary: No spray cures this, so prevention is everything!
cultural.how: Plant wilt-resistant varieties (e.g. Arka Nidhi, Arka Keshav, Arka Neelkanth, Pusa Anupama; Swarna Shyamli and Swarna Pratibha are released for Zone I including HP), rotate with maize/wheat/rice/soybean and use Brassica green manure.
cultural.evidence: NIPHM-Brinjal and ICAR records; check local availability of each variety. Wilt incidence reached 90-100% in the worst HP fields.

cultural.summary: Keep the soil drier and hotter for the germ!
cultural.how: Avoid waterlogging (the germ spreads in irrigation water, soil and tools). Solarize with 125 micron clear polythene for 8-10 weeks in March-June.

cultural.summary: Remove infected plants early to protect the rest!
cultural.how: Uproot infected plants as soon as you see symptoms and destroy them away from the field (not in compost).

biological.summary: A friendly soil fungus that crowds out root germs!
biological.how: Mix 1 kg Trichoderma viride 1% WP with 25 kg well-rotted FYM, broadcast over one acre and irrigate immediately.
biological.evidence: Dose from NIPHM-Brinjal. For Phytophthora, a bioagent + raised bed + mulch package roughly halved severity versus grower practice but still used fungicides (IIHR 2021), so this is risk reduction, not a cure.

botanical.summary: Neem cake in the soil deters nematodes and soil pests!
botanical.how: Apply neem cake at 100 kg per acre at transplanting (second split 30 days later in chilli beds).

cultural.summary: Beetles, grubs and pupae sit exposed on the leaves!
cultural.how: Pick and destroy grubs, pupae and adults from skeletonised leaves.

biological.summary: Natural enemies keep hadda in check!
biological.how: Avoid harming the parasitoids Pediobius foveolatus and Tetrastichus ovularum (active March-July).
